rationale: The previous fan-out run was a harness failure: build_node configures nodes 1..5 but the probe created only two instances, so a message to pid 3 was routed to a missing node and the test panicked before emitting events. This successor builds all five instances and keeps the same ten-entry, trim-to-five, two-cursor simulation; no target evidence changed.

scope.description: Two-node in-process cluster with ten decided entries and trim to 5. Two subscriber cursors are simulated over the real read_decided_suffix outputs with the actor's fan-out arithmetic: a slow cursor at 1 (below compaction) and a fast cursor at 6.
assumptions: All produced messages are delivered until none remain; no ticks are called.
The fan-out loop reproduces actor.rs push_to_all_subs: min_next = min cursor, one read from min_next, start = cursor - min_next, one cursor step per element pushed.
excluded: Channel capacity and backpressure behaviour, snapshots, batching, and more than two subscribers.

experiment.prefix: Build nodes 1 and 2, settle, node1.try_become_leader(), settle, append Value(1..=10) with a full settle after each, then node1.trim(Some(5)) and settle. Emit setup with decided, compacted, slow_cursor=1 and fast_cursor=6. Run up to three fan-out rounds: min_next = min(slow, fast); read_decided_suffix(min_next); for each cursor in [slow, fast], start = cursor - min_next, push every element from start, incrementing that cursor per element. Emit fanout with the two token streams and final cursors.

comparisons.description: Predicted fast-subscriber stream: entry 10 is delivered for cursor 6 (skipping 7, 8, 9) and 10 is delivered again later, while 7 is never delivered.

experiment.revision_reason: The fan-out probe instantiated only pids 1 and 2 while build_node configures nodes 1..5, so routing a message to pid 3 panicked before any event. The successor builds all five instances; the ten-entry, trim-to-five scenario and the two simulated cursors are unchanged.
